text.p: Italian debt futures ended higher on the day but still well within their recent downtrend as nervousness over prospects for a possible delay in European economic and monetary union (EMU) continued to grip the market.
The lira managed to forge a path back towards the 1,000 barrier although it did not return to a three digit price against the mark, but its strength helped the bond market.

Analysts said several factors were continuing to eat away at BTPs, with uncertainty as the market awaited details of the proposed mini-budget, EMU concerns and then the global out outlook for interest rates over the longer term.

The June Btp future on LIFFE was 45 basis points up at 124.63 with support cited around 124.25 and resistance at 124.90. The November 2006 Btp ended 84 basis points up at 100.49, yielding 7.81 percent with a spread over the 10-year Bund of 187 basis points.
The most traded July 2006 Btp was 74 basis points higher at 105.52.

On the domestic front, Thursday brings the first six out of 11 sample Italian cities to publish their preliminary inflation data for March with five following on Friday. Forecasts are for a year on year rate of 2.3 percent from February's 2.4 percent.

Also on the domestic front, newspapers say the state's quarterly accounts are likely to be presented Thursday or Friday, which will indicate how large the government's planned mini-budget for 1997 will have to be.
